title: Evidence Entropy Minimization and AuthZ Preservation
author: Maya Chen
body:
Summary:
This playbook defines a consistent, low-entropy evidence capture and retention workflow for incidents that cross RBAC boundaries, invoke audit logging, or involve model-serving/data residency concerns. The goal is to minimize transformations (entropy) applied to evidence, preserve authorization state (AuthZ snapshots), and create verifiable evidence bundles suitable for security investigations, regulatory review, or legal hold.

Audience
- Security Incident Response (SIRT)
- Eng-SRE and Platform Oncall
- Legal and Compliance (evidence intake)
- Customer Success / SOC for tenant-specific incidents

Why low-entropy evidence matters
- Every canonicalization, log-formatting pass, or pipeline enrichment increases the risk of data loss, timestamp drift, and audit correlation breakage.
- Preserving original artifacts with signed manifests accelerates triage and reduces disputes during external audits.

Scope and applicability
- Applies to incidents touching: RBAC and entitlements, audit log integrity, data residency boundaries, private deployments, and model artifact access.
- Not a substitute for immediate containment or emergency legal holds; use in parallel with existing incident response playbooks.

Key principles
1) Preserve originals first: always capture raw artifacts (log segments, KV cache dumps, model bundle IDs, RBAC snapshots) before any parsing, masking, or enrichment.
2) Snapshot AuthZ state: capture the exact set of active entitlements and policy decisions at the incident time (see AuthZ Snapshot section).
3) Signed manifests: for each evidence bundle create a signed manifest (SHA-256 + ksign) that lists objects, checksums, timestamps, and access controls.
4) Immutable packaging: store evidence bundles in an immutable bucket/airgap staging area with object lock (WORM) where supported.
5) Minimize application-layer transforms: do enrichment in a copy workspace, never on originals.
6) Retention mapping by classification: map evidence to retention schedules that balance investigatory needs and residency constraints.

Ownership and escalation
- Primary owner: Security Forensics (security)
- Secondary owner: Eng-SRE (oncall)
- Legal intake owner: Legal Evidence Intake Team
- Pager escalation: SIRT primary oncall -> Head of Security -> Legal (if subpoena or cross-border data)

Required SLOs and thresholds
- Evidence capture start: within 30 minutes of incident triage (high-severity)
- Raw artifact preservation confirmation: within 2 hours
- Manifest generation and signature: within 4 hours
- Chain-of-custody stub entry created in evidence index: within 4 hours

AuthZ Snapshot (what to collect)
- Effective user entitlements (list of roles, scopes) for the implicated identity at incident time
- Recent policy-eval audit log entries (±5 minutes) for decisions related to the event
- Applicable feature flags and rollout state
- Service-to-service tokens and short-lived credentials active at time of incident (token IDs, not plaintext credentials)
- Admin session metadata (session id, principal, MFA assertion id)

Minimum artifact list per bundle
- Raw application logs (exact file(s) or stream segment)
- Audit log slices (authorization decisions, token use, role changes)
- Model artifact identifiers (model-id, checksum, version manifest)
- Container/k8s pod snapshot (yaml manifest + pod logs)
- Host forensic snapshot (ps, network sessions) where allowed by policy
- RBAC policy source at time-of-incident (git commit id or policy blob)

Packaging format and manifest (example)
- Naming convention: evidence/{incident_id}/{bundle_version}/originals/{artifact}
- Manifest file: manifest-<incident_id>-v<version>.json (signed)
- Manifest fields (minimum): incident_id, bundle_version, created_at, artifacts[], checksums{}, signer, signature, retention_class

Example manifest (do not edit original; included here for reference):
{
  "incident_id": "INC-2026-0042",
  "bundle_version": "v1",
  "created_at": "2026-01-10T14:23:08Z",
  "artifacts": ["app/logs/service-A/2026-01-10T14-20-00-14-30-00.log", "audit/evt-0001234.ndjson"],
  "checksums": {"app/logs/service-A/2026-...log": "sha256:abcd..."},
  "signer": "security-proof-key-1",
  "signature": "MEUCIQ...",
  "retention_class": "investigation-7y"
}

Storage and evidence lifecycle
- Staging area: s3://evidence-staging/ (object-lock enabled) or equivalent GCS bucket with retention policy.
- Canonical archive: s3://evidence-archive/<jurisdiction>/ (immutable, cross-region replication disabled unless approved)
- Short retention for ephemeral test tenants: 90 days; standard incident: 2 years; regulated customers: 7 years (map per contract)
- Evidence read-only mode: all archive buckets must be mounted readonly for forensic access requests.

Retention matrix (summary):
| Classification         | Default retention | Regulatory override | Storage location                         |
|------------------------|-------------------|----------------------|------------------------------------------|
| Ephemeral test tenant  | 90d               | N                     | evidence-archive-us/test                 |
| Standard incident      | 2y                | If requested by legal | evidence-archive-us/standard             |
| Regulated customer     | 7y                | Required              | evidence-archive-eu or evidence-archive-us |
| Legal hold (case ID)   | Indefinite until release | N/A            | legal-hold-archive/<case-id>             |

Evidence intake procedure (step-by-step)
1) Triage and scope: SIRT determines impacted services and tenant scope.
2) Preserve originals: use the preservation CLI to copy artifacts to staging with object-lock.
   - Example: SIRT preservation CLI
     - curl -X POST https://forensics.internal/api/preserve
       -H 'Content-Type: application/json'
       -d '{"incident_id":"INC-2026-0042","paths":["/var/log/service-A.log","/var/log/audit.ndjson"]}'
3) Generate manifest: run evidence-manifest-generator --incident INC-2026-0042 --version v1 --sign-key security-proof-key-1
4) Snapshot AuthZ: execute authz-snapshot --principal user:alice --window 5m --out authz-snapshot-INC-2026-0042.json
5) Verify checksums: evidence-verify --manifest manifest-INC-2026-0042.json
6) Ship to canonical archive: evidence-ship --from staging --to archive --manifest manifest-INC-2026-0042.json --jurisdiction us
7) Update evidence index: add entry to EVIDENCE_INDEX (immutable event stream) with bundle id and chain-of-custody reference.

Tooling and CLI references
- preservation service: forensics.internal (POST /api/preserve)
- manifest generator: evidence-manifest-generator (binary in /opt/forensics/bin)
- authz snapshot: authz-snapshot (integrates with the policy engine)
- verification: evidence-verify (wraps sha256 + signer verification)
- index: internal kafka topic evidence.index (compact, encrypted)

Auditing and verification
- All manifest signatures must verify using the security key registry. Keys are rotated quarterly.
- Hashes use SHA-256, hex encoded and recorded in the manifest.
- Evidence-indexing emits a compact event: {incident_id, bundle_id, signer, archived_at, retention_class, archive_path}. Keep a copy in the SECURE_LOGSTORE for at least 5 years.

Cross-border and data residency considerations
- Do not replicate raw tenant artifacts across jurisdictions unless explicitly approved by data-residency owners and Legal.
- For regulated customers with EU residency requirements, create archive in evidence-archive-eu and restrict access to EU-only principals.

Privacy and redaction guidance
- Original artifacts must be preserved. Any redaction required for privacy must be performed on a copy and recorded as an enriched artifact with its own manifest and provenance entry.

Chain-of-custody example entry (human-readable)
- Timestamp: 2026-01-10T16:04:00Z
- Actor: maya.chen (SIRT)
- Action: preserved -> s3://evidence-staging/INC-2026-0042/v1/originals/service-A.log
- Hash: sha256:abcd1234...
- Manifest: s3://evidence-staging/INC-2026-0042/v1/manifest-INC-2026-0042-v1.json

Operational checklists
- Pre-capture checklist (SIRT):
  - Confirm scope, severity, and legal holds required
  - Notify Eng-SRE and Legal intake if tenant/regulatory data is involved
  - Acquire temporary write lock on affected service logs if possible
- Post-capture checklist:
  - Verify manifest signature and checksums
  - Tag evidence with retention_class and jurisdiction in index
  - Escalate to Legal for cross-border incidents

When to redact vs keep raw
- Redact only if required by law or when preparing evidence for external stakeholders. Keep raw in an internal locked archive.

Playbook examples (common scenarios)
- Role Escalation: user obtains unauthorized admin role via misconfigured feature flag
  - Capture flag state, policy commits, admin session logs, and audit decision logs.
- Model Exfiltration Attempt: anomalous large model download from a private deployment
  - Capture model artifact identifiers, network flow, presigned url history, and RBAC evals for the presigned token.

Compliance evidence workflow and handoff
- For evidence required by regulators or legal, create a packaged deliverable: signed-manifest + copy of artifacts + chain-of-custody and a short README describing scope and collection steps. Use legal-hold-archive for long-term preservation.

Retention release and destruction
- Evidence may only be released from legal-hold by explicit Legal signoff.
- Standard archival deletion: automate deletion when retention period expires; keep manifest index for an additional 2 years per policy.

Frequently asked questions
Q: What if we accidentally edit an original artifact?
A: Immediately record the edit in the chain-of-custody, preserve a copy of the pre-edit artifact if available, and escalate to SIRT lead.

Q: Can we encrypt evidence at rest?
A: Yes. All staging and archive buckets must be encrypted using KMS keys that are auditable. Key usage must be recorded in manifest metadata.

Appendix A: Example commands
- Preserve path:
  curl -X POST https://forensics.internal/api/preserve -H 'Authorization: Bearer <token>' -H 'Content-Type: application/json' -d '{"incident_id":"INC-2026-0042","paths":["/var/log/service-A.log","/var/log/audit.ndjson"]}'
- Generate manifest:
  evidence-manifest-generator --incident INC-2026-0042 --version v1 --path ./staging/INC-2026-0042/v1 --sign-key security-proof-key-1
- Verify:
  evidence-verify --manifest ./staging/INC-2026-0042/v1/manifest-INC-2026-0042-v1.json

Appendix B: Roles and contacts
- Security Forensics: security-forensics@redwood.ai (oncall roster in PagerDuty)
- Eng-SRE: eng-sre-oncall@redwood.ai
- Legal Evidence Intake: legal-evidence@redwood.ai
